findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan vent in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation. 
2. The outer surface area behind the soda nozzles was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The standing freezer by the cook line was observed to have ice buildup.

The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed. Ensure the surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas in the facility were observed to be in need of repair:

1. The space between the wall and handwashing sink by the cook line freezer was observed to be in need of caulking/sealing.
2. The space between the wall and three-compartment sink was observed to be in need of caulking/sealing.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the spaces mentioned above are caulked/sealed for easy cleaning and to prevent water from entering the spaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

Multiple employees were observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to actuate the paper towel dispensers. Multiple options were discussed with the PIC for handling this situation but the primary idea is that the bare hands should not be used to actuate this machine. Education conducted to correct. Ensure safe hand washing procedures are used at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The soap dispenser in the men’s bathroom is observed empty during this inspection. The dispenser was replaced during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sinks in both bathrooms are observed pulling away from the wall and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair (re-caulk) prior to the next routine inspection and to maintain the surfaces smooth and easily cleanable at all times. Ensure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces at all times in areas subject to foods or moisture.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival all of the sanitizers in the facility are observed at 0 ppm quat. New buckets were ran. These registered intermittently at 0-200 ppm. It appears that the dispenser is not properly mixing the solution and large amounts of the concentrate are being off gassed in the bubbles on top of the solution. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. For the short term the PIC was able to manually make a solution of sufficient concentration to remain operational. This is not a long term solution. A follow up is being set for three days to ensure that the machine is repaired/adjusted and compliance attained.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of this inspection allergen training certificates were not available for the certified food protection managers (CFPMs). The PIC is instructed to have all of the CFPMs complete allergen training and maintain copies of the certifications at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed the caulk seals on the mop sink, and both hand sinks in the kitchen to have areas where seal material is missing or is in need of being replaced. Replace caulk seals on these 3 sinks before the next routine inspection. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
